items.title: Intravascular imaging-guided PCI for complex lesions is linked to about half the stent thrombosis: meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (JACC: Advances)
items.summary: In 18 RCTs (18,975 patients) of complex PCI, IVUS- or OCT-guided stenting was linked to about half the stent thrombosis and to lower MACE and cardiac death vs angiography guidance, but the MACE benefit was mainly in Asian trials and several results lost significance after trim-and-fill (JACC: Advances, Oct 2026).
bullets: **JACC: Advances meta-analysis**: **intravascular imaging (IVUS/OCT)-guided vs angiography-guided PCI** in **complex coronary lesions**.
**18 RCTs, 18,975 patients**; frequentist random-effects plus Bayesian analyses.
**Stent thrombosis**: RR **0.52** (0.35-0.78): about **half**. **MI**: RR 0.87 (0.76-0.998); **clinically driven TLR**: RR 0.72 (0.51-0.999).
Within imaging-guided arms (6 studies), achieving imaging-defined stent optimisation vs not was linked to fewer MACE/TVF events: RR **0.41** (0.26-0.62), I²=62.7%. This is a within-arm association.
**Geographic interaction** (P<0.01): the MACE benefit came mainly from **Asian trial populations**.

Limits: **publication bias**; after trim-and-fill, MACE, cardiac death, MI and TLR lost significance, and cardiac death, MI and TLR were sensitive to single trials. **Stent thrombosis** (high certainty, I² 0.7%) is the most robust result.
